text: Every floor has to send its weight somewhere. So which beams actually feel this cat?
The piece of floor each beam carries is called its tributary area.
First, check the panel's shape. Divide the long side by the short side.
Eighteen by six is a ratio of three. More than two means a one-way slab.
The load runs straight across to the two long beams. Each one carries half the short span: a uniform load.
Now squish it closer to square. Twelve by nine is about one point three. Two or less means two-way.
Draw forty-five degree lines from every corner. Now the load flows to all four edges.
The short beams get triangles. The long beams get trapezoids.
Same floor, same load per square foot. Just a different shape, and a different load path.
Long and skinny, one way. Close to square, two ways.
